problem: Prior interactive navigation (NAMO) work relies on geometry-based planning, predefined skills, or quasi-static assumptions, and cannot rapidly identify unknown object dynamics (mass, friction, locked wheels) that vision alone cannot reveal.
motivation: Indoor objects such as boxes, carts and wheelchairs have irregular dynamics that determine whether they can be pushed or must be avoided. Identifying these dynamics needs physical interaction, and the identified dynamics must feed long-term planning decisions, not only control.
key_idea: Learn an object-invariant shared basis representation psi of planar SE(2) object dynamics in simulation via domain-adversarial meta-learning, adapt only a low-dimensional linear coefficient online, and use the resulting model inside MPPI for pushing and for deciding whether to push or go around.
insight: Splitting dynamics into a shared basis learned offline plus a small online-adapted linear coefficient gives fast adaptation with about 25 s of data and transfers from sim to real without retraining the object model. The baseline study shows the learned psi (MSE 0.4271 after adaptation, from 1.3131 before) beats a trigonometric basis (0.5720) and is slightly better than a residual-adaptive psi (0.4820). The MPPI rollouts also serve as a manipulability test.
method: Robot platform: Shmoobot, a ball-balancing robot with 3-DoF arms, a cascaded-PID balancing controller and Cartesian impedance arm control; controller input is u=[phi_x, phi_y, gamma] (lean angles and steering angle).

Decoupled dynamics: the robot model R is an MLP predicting robot acceleration and interaction force, and the object model O(x^o, Gamma^o; c) ≈ psi(x^o, Gamma^o) a(c) predicts SE(2) object acceleration. Only a(c) is adapted online.

DAIML with multi-step loss: psi is trained on sim teleoperation data (box, cart, wheelchair with randomized mass, friction and wheel constraints). An adversarial discriminator h removes condition-specific information from psi, and a covariance-weighted multi-step loss improves long-horizon prediction.
Online adaptation: a recursive update law estimates a(c) with an adaptive covariance-like matrix P. R is fine-tuned with about 5 min of real teleoperated data, with force estimated as J·tau.
MPPI adaptive pushing: S=500 rollouts, horizon T=30, 10 Hz, lambda=0.7. Cost is the object pose distance to the goal plus action-magnitude and action-smoothness penalties.
Collision-free navigation: A* global planner plus differentially-flat local trajectory optimization for the ball-balancing robot.

Object planner: picks a collision-free object goal within a 2m×2m area, then refines it via MPPI rollouts. If the rollout-predicted object displacement stays below a threshold (K<0.3), the object is registered as an obstacle and the path is replanned.

setting.backbone: MLP robot model R + DNN basis psi with linear coefficients (trained from scratch) inside MPPI; A* planner
setting.training_data: Simulated teleoperation data in PyBullet for 3 object categories with randomized dynamics, plus 5 min of real robot data to fine-tune R
setting.observation: RealSense D435i RGB-D plus T265 tracking camera; AprilTags on object corners for object pose and size; pre-built map
setting.action_space: Low-level robot commands: lean angles phi_x, phi_y and steering angle gamma, which give arm end-effector placement
setting.privileged: Pre-built map; AprilTags on objects for pose estimation

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark is used. Reported results are model-prediction MSE (mean over 20 unseen objects: 1.3131 before adaptation, 0.4271 after; trigonometric baseline 0.5720; residual baseline 0.4820), real pushing offsets (0.067 m, 0.124 m, 0.164 m for Goals 1-3), and a qualitative real-world NAMO demo.
results: The adaptive model reduces average MSE on 20 unseen objects from 1.3131 to 0.4271, beating a trigonometric basis (0.5720) and a residual-adaptive basis (0.4820). Real-world pushing reaches goals with mean offsets of 0.067/0.124/0.164 m. Shmoobot pushes a 2.8 kg box out of the way and detours around a locked 11.9 kg wheelchair.
limitations: Evaluation is small-scale and qualitative: one NAMO demo, no success-rate statistics and no comparison with other interactive navigation methods.
Requires AprilTags on objects, a pre-built map and planar SE(2) dynamics only, with three object categories in training; door opening and more complex tasks are left as future work.
